{{Quote|Rescinding previous consumer documentation that guaranteed a "lifetime" of reliability in their after-market astromech hover rockets, Industrial Automaton has now capped the warranty at 20 standard years. ''[&hellip;]'' The decision stems from a costly out-of-court settlement IA paid to a Sump port worker injured by a falling droid.|HoloNet News report|<ref name="HNN" />}}
'''Sump''' was [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Koradin sector/Legends|Koradin sector]]. It was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the easily-manipulated [[Nuknog/Legends|Nuknog]] [[Species/Legends|species]], the leaders of which sold their world to a consortium of [[Mining/Legends|mining]] corporations around [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]]. The Nuknog were then essentially reduced to [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]], working for [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] at offworld mines and [[Factory/Legends|factories]] for no pay while Sump was gradually polluted.

When a pair of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] eventually arrived on the planet in search of a wanted criminal, the plight of the Nuknog was made known to the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], which ordered the mining corporations to cease their operations on Sump. The planet's economy was subsequently left in ruins, and, despite Republic relief efforts that brought [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]] supplies to the starving Nuknog and offered to help them rebuild their [[Farm/Legends|agricultural]] industry, the distrustful natives were ultimately unwilling to help themselves, and by the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] interest in their situation waned.

==Description==
Sump was a [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="UAA" /> located in the [[Sump system/Legends|Sump system]], a part of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories']] [[Koradin sector/Legends|Koradin sector]].<ref name="EAOC" /> It was situated on the [[Lipsec Run/Legends|Lipsec Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]], which linked it to the [[Virgillia system/Legends|Virgillia]] and [[Keskin system/Legends|Keskin systems]].<ref name="TEA" /> Sump was a [[Water/Legends|humid]]<ref name="UAA" /> [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|urban world]]<ref name="AotCIllustratedCompanion" /> that featured several [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] on its surface. Eventually, the planet's ecosystem became polluted, leading to the creation of vast, [[Poison/Legends|toxic]] [[Swamp/Legends|marshes]] that could not sustain life.<ref name="UAA" />

==History==
===A world sold===
[[Realspace/Legends|Space]] surrounding Sump had been widely [[Scout/Legends|explored]] between [[3000 BBY]] and [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]].<ref name="TEA" /> Around the latter [[Standard year/Legends|year]], leaders of the planet's easily-manipulated native [[Nuknog/Legends|Nuknog]] [[Species/Legends|species]] made a deal with a consortium of unscrupulous offworld [[Mining/Legends|mining]] corporations wherein the Nuknog would cede control over their world in exchange for employment, [[Foodstuff/Legends|food]], and modest accommodations. The corporations subsequently put the natives to work in mines and processing [[Factory/Legends|factories]], where they performed tasks that were deemed too hazardous for offworld personnel.<ref name="UAA" />

The Nuknog were left unpaid for their work, [[Diet/Legends|ate]] leftovers, and [[Sleep/Legends|slept]] in tight prefabricated military [[Barracks/Legends|barracks]]. The mining industry eventually polluted Sump, and meanwhile, countless Nuknog [[Death/Legends|perished]] due to low-quality equipment and mining accidents. For the following [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]], changes to the mining contracts led to Sump and the de facto [[Slavery/Legends|enslaved]] Nuknog changing the company that owned them, and the plight of the planet's natives did not catch the attention of the wider [[galactic community]]<ref name="UAA" /> despite at least one Nuknog,<ref name="JPEndnotes1">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2010/12/endnotes-for-star-wars-jedi-path-part-1.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Jedi Path (part 1 of 4)}}</ref> [[Gal-Stod Slagistrough]], being a member of the offworld [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]]<ref name="TJP">[[The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force (real-life book)|''The Jedi Path: A Manual for Students of the Force'']]</ref> by [[990 BBY]].<ref name="JPEndnotes1" />

===Republic sympathy===
[[File:Nuknog_UAA.png|thumb|left|300px|Sump was the homeworld of the Nuknog species.]]
The situation changed when a pair of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] visited Sump during the search for a wanted criminal. The [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] became aware of the mistreatment of the Nuknog, and the Republic's [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] ordered the mining corporations to end their operations on the planet and repay the Nuknog several centuries' worth of lost wages. Amid the controversy, the corporations dissolved, abandoning the mines and factories on Sump and leaving the natives unable to feed themselves. The planet eventually became a dilapited locale that few offworlders cared to visit.<ref name="UAA" />

Sympathy for the starving Nuknog ran high in the Republic, leading relief workers to bring emergency food supplies to Sump and to offer to help the Nuknog rebuild their homeworld's devastated [[Farm/Legends|agricultural]] industry. The distrustful Nuknog, however, while accepting the food, instead blamed the Republic for their situation and demanded that the government supply them with food and other necessities in perpetuity. When it became apparent that Sump's natives were unwilling to put in the work themselves to help alleviate their plight, the public sympathy for the Nuknog disappeared. By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|events]] preceding the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the problems of the Nuknog on Sump no longer held any interest for the Senate or [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] at large, which made for another reason for the Nuknog to resent the Republic.<ref name="UAA" />

===Into the Clone Wars===
At some point by [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="22 BBY">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|55|business/1359_2.html|IA Caps Droid Rocket Warranty at 20 Years}} is set on the [[Great ReSynchronization|date]] "13:5:9," which corresponds to [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] per the reasoning [[Template:YearMathGRS|here]].</ref> an [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] manufactured by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] experienced a malfunction in its [[Rocket booster/Legends|hover rockets]] and fell down, injuring a worker at a port on Sump. The incident resulted in the company paying a costly out-of-court settlement to the worker and was eventually noted on the [[Great ReSynchronization|date]] 13:5:9 in an issue of the [[HoloNet News CoCo District Edition|CoCo District Edition]] of the [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]].<ref name="HNN">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|55|business/1359_2.html|IA Caps Droid Rocket Warranty at 20 Years}}</ref>

Sump remained outside of the Republic's territory during the Clone Wars,<ref name="TEA" /> although during the first campaigns of the conflict in 22 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]] the [[Nineteenth Army|Nineteenth Sector Army]] of the Republic was nevertheless tasked with engaging the [[Confederacy military/Legends|military forces]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] in the planet's vicinity.<ref name="EGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> By [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], Sump remained undecided on its affiliation to either the Republic or the Confederacy.<ref name="FF">{{FactFile|139|WOR 1-2|Worlds of the Clone Wars}}</ref> The planet was also situated outside of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] borders by [[17 BBY/Legends|17 BBY]].<ref name="EGTW" />

==Inhabitants==
{{Main|Nuknog/Legends}}
[[File:Ark_Roose_Card_FC.png|thumb|right|300px|The podracer Ark Roose hailed from Sump.]]
Sump was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the Nuknog, a species of [[Reptile/Legends|reptilian]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] that spoke the [[Nuknog (language)|Nuknog]] [[Language/Legends|language]]. The Nuknog barely managed to survive on their polluted homeworld. The average life expectancy of a Nuknog was nearly doubled if they made their home off Sump, and therefore, although it was a luxury that few of the planet's natives could afford, most Nuknog jumped at the chance to leave their homeworld and never return. The Nuknog were easily tricked with promises of safe passage offworld, but they had few skills to offer in return. In order to just leave Sump, those Nuknog who managed to depart frequently bought passage aboard passing [[Starship/Legends|starships]] by selling themselves into slavery.<ref name="UAA" />

The [[Private investigator/Legends|private investigator]] [[Slyther Bushforb/Legends|Slyther Bushforb]]<ref name="DB Bushforb">{{DB|character|slytherbushforb|Bushforb, Slyther}}</ref> and the [[Podracer (profession)/Legends|podracer]] [[Ark Roose/Legends|Ark Roose]]<ref name="NEGTC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> were both Nuknog from Sump who had made their way offworld,<ref name="DB Bushforb" /> with the Nuknog government only allowing the latter to participate in the [[Galactic Podracing Circuit/Legends|Galactic Podracing Circuit]] for promotional reasons.<ref name="NEGTC" /> The population of the Sump [[Star system/Legends|system]] around [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]] numbered between 500 million and one billion.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
Sump was first mentioned in the [[2000]] reference book ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]'' by [[Kristin Lund]].<ref name="Inside">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]''</ref> The first visual depiction of the planet was on a [[2001]] map of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' galaxy designed by [[James King]] and [[Laurence Butler]] and included with the [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 1|first issue]] of ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'' magazine.<ref name="FF1">{{FactFile|1|[[:File:Galaxymap3.jpg|Galaxy Map Poster]]}}</ref> "Sump" was erroneously used in the [[2002]] [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 26|twenty-sixth issue]] of ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File]]'' magazine as the species name of the Nuknog podracer [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] Ark Roose.<ref name="FF26">{{FactFile|26|POD 1-2|Podracer Pilots}}</ref> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed the Sump system, and therefore the planet itself, in grid square I-18.<ref name="TEA" />
